findings.evidence: The delta spec says "After an integration repair or derived merge". The diff touches only integration_contour.py and task_content_identity.py. post_review_finalization.py:583-584 still raises RederivationFailed("re-derivation changed the task-content identity") when equivalent_proofs fails. That is exactly the case where main changed a task path, as in scenario "Main touched a task path". design.md says "Finalize needs no change", but nothing makes the derived-merge path use main_only_integration.
findings.summary: The spec requires gate evidence to survive a main-only integration after an integration repair or a derived merge. The candidate implements the proof only in integration_contour.advance_after_repair. The derived-merge re-derivation path is unchanged and still rejects any main change to a task path.

findings.evidence: The spec says "THEN fresh developer semantic verification is required through handoff". advance_after_repair prints "receipt reset after integration repair: …" and falls through to the existing return-to-review branch. The new test asserts state == "review-pending". design.md says "returns to review as today", which differs from the spec's handoff wording.
findings.summary: Scenarios 2 and 3 say the receipt is reset or fresh developer semantic verification is required through handoff. The implementation only logs the reason to stderr and calls return_to_review (review-pending). Nothing in the diff resets the developer receipt or requires a handoff.
